name: EU Blue Card (Blaue Karte EU)

requirements.blocker_text: This requires a confirmed job offer matching your qualification level from a German employer.
requirements.fix_path: Secure a qualifying job offer from a German employer.

requirements.blocker_text: This requires a recognised university degree (checked via anabin/ZAB against your home institution).
requirements.fix_path: Obtain formal recognition of your degree via the ZAB/anabin database if it isn't automatically recognised.

requirements.blocker_text: This requires a gross annual salary of at least €50,700 (2026 figure — 50% of the annual pension-insurance contribution ceiling, which re-baselines every 1 January).
requirements.fix_path: Negotiate a higher salary, or check eligibility for the reduced shortage-occupation/graduate/IT threshold.

requirement_groups.name: Shortage occupation, recent graduate, or IT specialist (reduced threshold)

requirements.blocker_text: This requires a confirmed job offer matching your qualification level from a German employer.
requirements.fix_path: Secure a qualifying job offer from a German employer.

requirements.blocker_text: This requires either a role in a shortage occupation, a degree awarded within the last 3 years, or (for IT specialists without a matching degree) at least 3 years of relevant professional experience within the last 7 years.
This requires a gross annual salary of at least €45,934.20 (2026 figure — 45.3% of the annual pension-insurance contribution ceiling).

evidence_required.document: Degree recognition (anabin/ZAB) or equivalent proof of qualification
Employment contract meeting the applicable salary threshold
Federal Employment Agency approval (for offers below €4,225/month gross)

outcome.duration_length: up to 4 years, or contract duration + 3 months if shorter

sources.title: EU Blue Card - Make it in Germany (Federal Government portal)

notes: Highest-value counterfeit-figure catch in the Germany dataset. 2026 thresholds are €50,700 (standard) and €45,934.20 (shortage/graduate/IT) — pegged as exactly 50% and 45.3% of the 2026 pension-insurance contribution ceiling of €101,400/year, confirmed via Deutsche Rentenversicherung. Multiple sources still show 2025's stale €48,300/€43,750 figures as if current for 2026 — a direct parallel to the UK Skilled Worker £38,700-vs-£41,700 case, except here the whole THRESHOLD moves every January 1, not just occasionally. This is exactly the NationalVariable + formula-value pattern the schema was built for (see schema-v1.md §3, Portugal D7 stress test) — value stored here as a literal 2026 figure PLUS a formula annotation, since the schema's requirement.value field doesn't yet have a first-class formula_ref/ratio structure wired into the validator; a real gap, flagged rather than faked. pr_after_months (21) assumes B1 German — the settlement timeline under §18c(2) AufenthG is 27 months at basic/A1 German, reduced to 21 months at B1. IMPORTANT CORRECTION: the commonly-cited '33 months' figure (still on some English-language BMI FAQ pages) is stale — it was the PRE-2023-reform figure (33/27 months), superseded by the current 27/21 months since the March 2024 reform. This is a rare case where even an official English-language government page lags the German statute — flagged explicitly since it's the exact failure mode this product exists to catch, this time inside tier-1 sourcing itself. citizenship_after_months (81) = 21 months to settlement + standard 60-month naturalisation residence requirement, though Blue Card holders' settlement time likely also counts toward the naturalisation clock — not yet modeled precisely, flagged as an open question rather than asserted as fact.
